experiments.name: Titration: HCl vs NaOH
experiments.theory: In this experiment, we determine the concentration of a Strong Acid (HCl) by titrating it with a Strong Base (NaOH) using Phenolphthalein as an indicator.

steps.hint: Ensure the stopcock is closed and fill the burette with 0.1M NaOH to exactly the 0.00mL mark.
Use the pipette to transfer 25mL of 0.1M HCl to the conical flask.
Add 2-3 drops of Phenolphthalein indicator. It remains colorless in acid.
Slowly open the burette. Watch for the permanent pale pink endpoint at 25.00mL.

observations: The solution remained colorless when the indicator was added to HCl.
As NaOH was added, localized pink clouds appeared and disappeared.
At the endpoint, the solution turned a persistent pale pink color.

experiments.name: Chloride Ion Detection
experiments.theory: The presence of Chloride ions (Cl-) is confirmed by adding Silver Nitrate (AgNO3), which forms a white precipitate of Silver Chloride (AgCl).

steps.hint: Pour approximately 10mL of the unknown sample (NaCl solution) into the test tube.
Add a few drops of Silver Nitrate solution to the test tube.

observations: A thick, white curd-like precipitate forms immediately upon adding Silver Nitrate.
